description: Edit a trail's plan. A person edits the plan text, the release block (strategy, reason, the resources to create) or the breakdown (milestones and items). Pass at least one field. Any edit puts the plan back to `drafted`, so it needs approving again; a trail with no plan yet gets one this way. Not …

breakdown.description: The milestones and items a plan breaks the trail into. Nothing is filed while the plan is a draft; approving creates the milestones and files the items. `workKind` defaults to `code`.

items.description: The items, each in at most one milestone.
An item the plan proposes. Filed on the trail with source `plan` when the plan is approved.

assignee.description: Who works the item — an agent handle (`claude`, `cursor`, `copilot`, `jules`, `muse`, `grok`) or a person's email. `null`, the project's coding agent.

body.description: The item's description in markdown — what to do and how to tell it is done.

creates.description: On a `tracking` item, the tracking resources it creates, as `kind:key`. Every event, metric and alert rule the release lists that does not exist yet must be created by one.

milestone.description: The name of the breakdown milestone the item belongs to, or `null` for none.

anyOf.description: Triage priority of a queue item. The lowest tier is `nice_to_have` (not `low`) — carried over from the feature-request "importance" scale this priority set replaced.

shipsDark.description: Work that cannot sit behind a flag — a schema migration, an API contract change, a backfill. It lands first, backward compatible.

title.description: The item's title. A replan's approval matches items already on the trail by title and files only the new ones.

type.description: What to file the item as.

workKind.description: What kind of work an item on a trail is — `code` (a change to the product), `tracking` (events, metrics and alert rules to measure it), `marketing`, `research` or `ops`. Code and tracking items go to coding agents; marketing and research items are typically delegated to an assistant such as Muse or Grok, which picks them up over MCP (`ops list --owner muse`).

items.description: A milestone the plan proposes. Created when the plan is approved.

name.description: The milestone's name. Breakdown items name it in their `milestone`.

targetDate.description: The calendar day the milestone is meant to be done by (`YYYY-MM-DD`), or `null`.

handle.description: The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id.

marketing.description: The plan's marketing strategy — tracked, never executed. Every channel is also a breakdown item of the same title with `workKind` `marketing`, so it has an owner, a status and a place on the timeline.

brief.description: One or two lines on what it is.

channel.description: Where a marketing action on a trail's plan happens.

timing.description: When it lands: `before_release`, `at_release`, `at_full_rollout`, `after_goal`, or a milestone's name.

title.description: The breakdown item that tracks it (same title).

summary.description: Positioning and audience in a paragraph — who it is for and what it says.

release.description: How the trail ships. The person answers this while the plan is made; the build run creates exactly the resources listed (none for `straight_to_main`), and the Plan gate checks they exist.

flags.description: How each `gate` in `resources` is rolled out beyond its ramp — what it buckets on, the team stage, the item that removes it. One entry per gate.

bucketBy.description: What a flag hashes on — `user`, `org` (a B2B feature never shows half a team the new behaviour) or `device` (logged-out surfaces).

cleanup.description: The title of the breakdown item (`workKind` `code`) that removes the flag and its dead branch once it is at 100%.

internalFirst.description: Whether the project's members get it before any public percent (the team stage). On by default.

internalSkipReason.description: Why the team stage is skipped — required when `internalFirst` is false.

reason.description: One line on why this approach — risk, blast radius, reversibility.

resources.description: The flags, kill switches, experiments and tracking (events, metrics, alert rules) to create. No release tool for `straight_to_main`; the strategy fixes which release kinds must be present (a flag for `flag`, a flag and an experiment for `flag_experiment`, and so on). A trail may ship behind several flags; each `ships_behind` flag gets its own rollout, its resource's `rollout` or else this block's.

items.description: One resource the build run creates and links to the trail — a release tool or a piece of tracking.

key.description: The key or name the build run creates it under, e.g. `checkout.v2`.

kind.description: The resources a plan may list for the build to create — the release tools (a feature flag (`gate`), a kill switch, an experiment) and the tracking (an `event` to emit, a `metric` to define, an `alert_rule` to guard with).

role.description: What a resource is for on the trail — `ships_behind` (the flag the code ships behind), `rollback` (the kill switch that undoes it), `measures` (the experiment or metric that judges it), `guards` (an alert rule that watches it), `copy` (an i18n key it adds) or `touched` (anything else). The release gates and the release phase read these.

rollout.description: How the flag a trail ships behind is ramped after merge — the release controller's plan (see the design doc, the release controller). Part of the plan's release block; the project's defaults live in `trail-gates` `rollout`. The controller runs on the alerts cron, so a hold shorter than the cron interval rounds up to the next tick.

guards.description: What is watched while a step holds. The trail's `guards` alert-rule resources are watched too.

alertRuleIds.description: Alert rules (ids) whose firing during a step is a breach.

attributedErrors.description: Whether a new error attributed to the trail at high confidence is a breach.

experimentGuardrails.description: Whether a breached guardrail of the trail's measuring experiment is a breach.

holdMinutes.description: Minutes a step must stay healthy before the next one.
Minutes the team stage holds healthy before the first public step.

internal.description: The team stage before any public percent — the project's members are allowlisted on the flag (by email) and the step holds like any other. `null` or absent = no team stage.

minExposure.description: Evaluations a step must have served before it counts as healthy, so a quiet hour never passes as a green one. `0` = no floor.

policies.description: The three decisions the plan asks the owner, each with the project default pre-selected.

advance.description: Whether a healthy step advances by itself (`auto`) or waits for the owner to say so (`ask`).

afterFix.description: What happens when the fix merges — `resume` from the last healthy step, `ask` the owner first, or `restart` from the first step.

breachTimeoutMinutes.description: With `ask_then_pull_back`, minutes the owner has before the controller pulls back.

onBreach.description: What to do when a guard trips during a step — `pull_back` (pull the flag back, investigate and suggest a fix, tell the owner; the default), `ask_first` (ask the owner, only notify), or `ask_then_pull_back` (ask, and pull back after `breachTimeoutMinutes` with no answer).

steps.description: Percent steps, each above the one before, the last 100.

risks.description: What could go wrong, how it would be seen and how it is undone. Required once the plan ships behind a release tool or has more than two items.

items.description: One thing that could go wrong.

class.description: The failure class a risk belongs to — the checklist the plan run walks.

detect.description: The guard that would catch it, as `kind:key` (`alert_rule:…`, `metric:…`, `experiment:…`), listed in the plan or already existing. Required for a `high` risk.

impact.description: How bad it is if it happens.

mitigation.description: What the plan does to make it less likely, or `null`.

risk.description: What could go wrong, in a line.

rollback.description: How the risk is undone once it happens. The plan must carry the tool it names.

rollout.description: How the flag a trail ships behind is ramped after merge — the release controller's plan (see the design doc, the release controller). Part of the plan's release block; the project's defaults live in `trail-gates` `rollout`. The controller runs on the alerts cron, so a hold shorter than the cron interval rounds up to the next tick.

alertRuleIds.description: Alert rules (ids) whose firing during a step is a breach.

attributedErrors.description: Whether a new error attributed to the trail at high confidence is a breach.

experimentGuardrails.description: Whether a breached guardrail of the trail's measuring experiment is a breach.

Minutes the team stage holds healthy before the first public step.

internal.description: The team stage before any public percent — the project's members are allowlisted on the flag (by email) and the step holds like any other. `null` or absent = no team stage.

minExposure.description: Evaluations a step must have served before it counts as healthy, so a quiet hour never passes as a green one. `0` = no floor.

policies.description: The three decisions the plan asks the owner, each with the project default pre-selected.

advance.description: Whether a healthy step advances by itself (`auto`) or waits for the owner to say so (`ask`).

afterFix.description: What happens when the fix merges — `resume` from the last healthy step, `ask` the owner first, or `restart` from the first step.

breachTimeoutMinutes.description: With `ask_then_pull_back`, minutes the owner has before the controller pulls back.

onBreach.description: What to do when a guard trips during a step — `pull_back` (pull the flag back, investigate and suggest a fix, tell the owner; the default), `ask_first` (ask the owner, only notify), or `ask_then_pull_back` (ask, and pull back after `breachTimeoutMinutes` with no answer).

steps.description: Percent steps, each above the one before, the last 100.

strategy.description: How the trail ships, as the person chose it while the plan was made — `straight_to_main` (no flag), `flag`, `flag_experiment` (a flag measured by an experiment), `kill_switch` (a kill switch only), `flag_kill_switch`, or `other` (a free-text answer that fits none of those).
